message.content:
Hello! I'm here to share some insights from your recent lesson on proper fractions. The overall score for the lesson was 75%, with 21 out of 28 marks. 

One major strength of the lesson was the clear objective you set. You effectively communicated the lesson focus by stating, "Today we are studying proper fractions," and converting it into a student task by saying, "You have to write its fraction." This approach helped students understand what they needed to achieve, keeping their practice focused and aligned with the lesson goal.

Now, let's talk about a growth opportunity. Differentiation is an area where you can enhance student engagement. Since all students worked on the same task, consider introducing two levels of practice: one simpler task and one more challenging extension. This way, students can work at their own pace and ability level. An easy way to start is by preparing a basic counting task and an extension that involves comparing fractions. 

In closing, your intent to adjust pacing and give quieter students more time to respond is a great step forward. Keep up the good work, and continue to build on these strengths and growth areas. You're doing great!
